mentioned.quote: Risks stemming from possible malicious use of foundation AI models, such as generating content to facilitate cybercrime or child sexual exploitation
mentioned.note: p.8 table also lists 'Malware code' with likelihood and severity.

threshold.note: No capability or risk level for cyber that changes what Cohere does. p.7-8 table gives illustrative likelihood and severity for malware code only; p.14 box describes thresholds as an industry approach, not Cohere's.

response.note: No response is tied to a cyber threshold. p.12 revoking access from abusive accounts and p.13 blocklists and classifiers are general practice, not conditioned on a threshold (E1).

acc_decider.note: nothing to decide for this risk; p.15 CEO delegation to the Chief Scientist covers launch readiness generally, with no cyber threshold or response.

acc_external.note: p.16 'independent third-party penetration testing of model containers' tests the security of Cohere's systems; red teaming with external parties 'may include' (hedged). Neither tests cyber capability or a threshold response.

acc_unmet.note: p.16 says regressions are 'investigated and mitigated before deployment', a generic performance statement with no cyber response to fail.

mentioned.note: p.14-15 mention radiological and nuclear weapons and biorisk only inside a box describing 'one approach to risk assurance in the AI industry', and the text then says that research is immature; Cohere does not adopt it (E7).

threshold.note: Only the industry approach in the p.14-15 box; not adopted.
